subject: psychology
title: Psychopathology: Defining Abnormality
welcome_lead: What counts as 'abnormal'? Four definitions, four problems.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology definitions of abnormality: deviation from norms, failure to function, ideal mental health, statistical.
final_note: No single definition is enough — clinicians lean on several.

concepts.def: Behaviour rare in the population (e.g. IQ below 70).
Unable to cope with everyday demands.
Jahoda's six criteria for healthy functioning.
Proposed seven signs of failure to function.
Norms differ between cultures — affects all four definitions.

walkthroughs.body_html: If a trait sits more than two standard deviations from the mean it's statistically rare. IQ below 70 (around 2% of people) qualifies someone for intellectual disability. But high IQ is also rare and not abnormal — a key limitation.

Each society defines acceptable behaviour. Hallucinating in public breaks unwritten rules. But norms are culturally relative: hearing the voice of a deceased ancestor is normative in some cultures, pathological in others. Norms also change over time — homosexuality was in the DSM until 1973.

walkthroughs.h2: Failure to Function & Ideal Mental Health
walkthroughs.body_html: Rosenhan & Seligman (1989) listed signs like personal distress and unpredictability. Jahoda (1958) proposed six criteria for ideal mental health (self-attitudes, growth, integration, autonomy, perception of reality, mastery of environment). The bar is so high almost everyone is 'abnormal' by it.
